newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says deal with state raises EPS 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: KLM says deal with state raises EPS 20 pct.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Thursday a planned buy-back of KLM ordinary shares held by the Dutch government would lead to an increase in earnings per ordinary share of some 20 percent.

"A pro forma recalculation of earnings per ordinary share will, after implementation of the transaction in question, lead to an increase of some 20 percent in earnings per ordinary share," KLM said in a joint statement with the government.
KLM said that after the plannned transaction its cash balance would show a pro forma decline to 2.0 billion guilders from 2.3 billion on September 30.
These figures took into account some 700 million guilders in cash generated by the previously announced sale of preference shares in Northwest Airlines Corp., it said.
KLM said shareholders' equity would fall to a pro forma figure of 32 percent of total long-term capital as a result of the planned transaction from 37 percent on September 30.
Net interest-bearing debt would rise to a pro forma 130 percent of shareholders' equity from 95 percent, it added.
